title: The Energy–Flow Interface: A Unified Thermodynamic Interpretation of Dark Matter, Dark Energy, and the CMB — within the Grid–Higgs Field Framework
description: Proposes Energy–Flow Cosmology (EFC), in which dark matter, dark energy, and the CMB are thermodynamic phases of a single Grid–Higgs medium governed by an energy–flux field coupled to local entropy. The paper identifies convergent (DM), divergent (DE), and isothermal interface (CMB) regimes and outlines testable predictions linking CMB anisotropies, large‑scale structure, and the dark‑energy equation of state.

grid_higgs_lagrangian.description: Effective Lagrangian for the Grid–Higgs field \Phi with potential V that depends on the field and local entropy S, providing a thermodynamic degree of freedom.

energy_entropy_coupling.description: Divergence of the energy–flux field J^\mu equals the entropy derivative of the potential, partitioning spacetime into convergent (DM-like), null-flux (CMB-like), and divergent (DE-like) regimes.

key_results.main_finding: DM, DE, and the CMB emerge as convergent, divergent, and isothermal-interface phases of a single entropy-coupled energy–flow field embedded in a Grid–Higgs medium.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB temperature anisotropies exhibit a scale-dependent cross-correlation with mapped dark-matter density fields beyond ΛCDM expectations, due to interface oscillations coupling convergent and divergent zones.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint CMB–LSS analyses (e.g., Planck/Simons Observatory/ACT × DESI/KiDS/LSST) showing no excess cross-correlation after accounting for ΛCDM ISW and lensing templates.

sealed_predictions.statement: There is a weak but nonzero coupling between the present CMB temperature (TCMB) and the dark-energy equation-of-state w(z), producing correlated temporal or environmental modulations at the interface.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Precision constraints on TCMB–w(z) covariance from multi-probe reconstructions (SN, BAO, RSD, lensing) showing consistency with zero coupling within uncertainties.

sealed_predictions.statement: The ISW signal is phase-shifted relative to dark-matter surface/overdensity maps, reflecting interface dynamics between convergent and divergent flows.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic ISW–LSS cross-correlation phase analyses (e.g., with DESI/LSST) finding no measurable phase shift beyond ΛCDM predictions.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-SNR (≥10) CMB–LSS cross-correlation studies across 100 ≤ ℓ ≤ 1000 find no residual correlation beyond ΛCDM ISW+lensing templates at |r| < 0.01, ruling out interface-induced anisotropy coupling.

KC2: Joint constraints on TCMB and w(z) over 0 ≤ z ≤ 2 show TCMB–w(z) coupling consistent with exactly zero (and not merely weak) at high significance (≥5σ), contradicting the predicted nonzero coupling.
KC3: Tomographic ISW–LSS analyses detect phase alignment fully consistent with ΛCDM and exclude any additional phase shift at ≥5σ across multiple redshift bins.

KC4: A concrete EFC implementation in CLASS/GADGET-4 fails to simultaneously match the observed CMB power spectra and the matter power spectrum for any plausible V(Φ,S) and initial conditions, indicating internal inconsistency of the framework.

KC5: Robust null results for cross-correlations between CMB small-scale anisotropies and independently reconstructed dark-matter convergence maps (from weak lensing) after foreground and systematic mitigation, across multiple surveys and pipelines.
